title: The Divine Arrow and the Light of the Soul
english: The daughter is commanded to rejoice intensely and suddenly at the appearance of the strong and saving King.

"God feels for Judah like a warrior wielding a sword," effecting salvation in both ways: just as a bow was strung for a blessed erotic desire, and just as an excellent general feels for a sword, being a warrior, in order to strike down those set in opposition. It is also written about this in the forty-fourth Psalm: "Gird your sword upon your thigh, O Mighty One, with your beauty and your splendor, because of truth and gentleness and righteousness, and your right hand shall lead you wondrously" (Psalm 45:3). For how would the right hand not lead wondrously the one who has girded a sword upon his thigh, the Mighty One, paradoxically striking those being struck?

It is indeed his own to hear [the enemies] being told regarding his divine power: "You Ethiopians are wounded by my sword." For having been wounded by him saying these things, casting off the life of the Ethiopians, they shall take up immortality, as it might be said graciously: "The brightness of the Lord our God shall be upon us" (Psalm 18:10), since, having washed us of the cause of all good things, we were shown bright and white, according to the one speaking with boldness: "You shall wash me and I shall be whiter than snow" (Psalm 51:7).

But from where did the Ethiopians come, those being wounded for good so that they might be put to death regarding impiety, or having been born from the devil, desiring to do his lusts? For it has been said about him that he is black, because of the approaching dark ignorance and malice, as is shown in the book of repentance called the Shepherd, and in the Epistle of Barnabas.

And we also have been struck saving-ly by the living and active Word, about whom it has been written: "The Word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword" (Hebrews 4:12), so that having been put to death in the flesh, we might be made alive in the spirit. And let us be struck also by the chosen arrow, sent from the drawn bow; for thus we shall be raised up, happening to be children of Zion upon the generations of the Greeks.

Many, being children and sons of the Greeks, strove according to the dogmas of piety, as to leave behind many writings; but they were overwhelmed when the ecclesiastical men of God rose up against them.

Let us overturn the contentious arguments of those with confidence, saying: 'The weapons of our warfare are not fleshly but are powerful in God, demolishing arguments and lifting up every height against the knowledge of God' (2 Cor 10:4-5). When the children of Zion rise up against the Greeks, the Lord, having accomplished this, will be 'over them' (Zech 9:14), uniting those who rise up with those against whom they rise up, as they are prepared to reign with one mind and one judgment, having created the Greek and the Jew into one new man.

And he will go forth like a flash of lightning, and the Lord God of hosts will sound the trumpet and will go forth in the fury of his indignation; the Lord God of hosts will protect them (Zech 9:14-15). When God has drawn the bow against Judah, a flash like lightning will go forth, piercing and striking toward divine love, so as to become the light of the world, which is able to be called a perfect soul or a glorious Church: 'I am wounded by love.' And it is not only there that the things sent from the divine bow are luminous; in Habakkuk it is said toward God: 'Your arrows shall go forth as light, into the brightness of lightning of your weapons' (Hab 1:8). There is no difference between saying it in the plural or the singular; for we take generally a flash going forth like lightning, of which kinds there are many among the individual flashes.

The word piercing toward desire, taking up the virtues according to kind and the doctrines according to part, is a flash in the general sense, while specific ones exist regarding each virtue and each doctrine of words, and for this reason they are named as flashes in the plural. Furthermore, just as one flash goes forth like lightning and many [go forth] into light according to Habakkuk, so all things sent from the bow drawn by God are bright arrows. And this is Judah.

It has been made clear previously that these things are announced concerning the one rising out of the tribe of Judah, the Savior. When the divine flash goes forth like lightning so that the inner man and the eyes of the heart may be enlightened, the Lord God of hosts sounds the trumpet, awakening also the inner hearing, so that having received the perception of the existing benefit, one may respond gratefully: 'The instruction of the Lord opens my ears' (Ps 119:16), after he has given me the habit of hearing. And see whether not by thought...

title: The Trumpet of Truth and the Armor of Light
english: The thing given by God is one trumpet and another lightning. For since the things announced clearly, piercingly, and loudly are heard, they are likened to a trumpet; but since they enlighten the mind, being the eye of the soul, they resemble lightning.

Just as all the divine things are bright and loud for those being benefited by free will and for ourselves, so a warning becomes against those turning back easily; whence it is appropriate to compare the one coming like a lightning bolt to the Lord Almighty blowing the trumpet, that the benefactor might be shaken in warning, with much goodness being presented by God walking in a storm of warning, so that he might not be completely cast out, the warning being at times corrected, as it happened regarding the Ninevites (Jonah 3:4).

For having said the one warning: 'In yet three days Nineveh shall be overturned' (Jonah 3:4), it seemed appropriate to shake them in warning and to cause them to turn, so that the place of repentance, given outside of the warning, might make those who had ceased from what they previously were doing to repent. In this way also Adam, as soon as he heard the voice of his wife being deceived by the serpent, received a sense of a branch of the Lawgiver, so to speak: 'I heard the voice of your feet walking' (Gen 3:11), before the transgression, being present and conversing.

And indeed, [the Lord] is not departing from the Jews when they sincerely kept the law and ministered to the one who gave it, nor has he entirely abandoned them to walk in a storm of warning, saying concerning them: 'I have left my house, I have abandoned my inheritance' (Jer 12:7). The abandonment is clearly shown, Jesus saying in the Gospel: 'Behold, your house is left to you' (Luke 19:42).

The purpose and the end are shown to be for the good of those being left, from the coming of: 'And the Lord Almighty shall go in a storm of his warning,' 'The Lord Almighty shall protect them.' For when it seemed to depart in warning, he helped just so, putting forward for them his invincible shield, concerning which it is said in the Hymns to the one being benefited: 'His truth shall surround you as a weapon' (Ps 5:12). Since it is said nearby how the Lord Almighty blows the blessings by him clearly and loudly, scriptural testimonies regarding this [are gathered]...

The Holy Spirit protects the herald of the truth, raising his voice like a trumpet, so that his teaching, which he brings to war, might rouse those fighting for God against those arrayed militarily against them, and also to call them to the festive assemblies. These things lie in the God-breathed oracles, sometimes with enigma, sometimes in historical narrative.

To show that blowing the trumpet means making things manifest, the words spoken by Jesus to those wishing to give gifts to the poor in the nearby region are sufficient: 'When you do alms, do not sound a trumpet before you.' For he wants this virtue to be practiced in secret, because vainglory is contrary to it and the praise-seeking is clearly performing it; but the command forbidding it is also transgressed: 'What you hate, do not do to another.' For to give gifts to those in need—so I phrase it—is, unfortunately, not to be a friend to the one being benefited, since the giver follows him and does that which he himself does not wish to suffer.

Therefore, when the Lord Almighty enlightens those being helped by him, making manifest what he grants, he blows in a trumpet, defending those well-disposed, so that they may remain unassailable and unharmed, surrounding them clothed in the invincible shield, having put on the whole armor of their ruler and king.

It would also be for us 'to put on the weapons of the light' and 'to take up the shield of faith,' so as to say with boldness: 'You are my help and my defender; my God, do not delay.' [Zach. IX, 15–16: And they shall devour them and subdue them with stones of the sling, and they shall pour out their blood like wine and fill as a bowl for the altar. And the Lord shall save them in that day, as a flock of his people, because the holy stones roll upon his earth.]

God, having set the Jew like a bow and having raised up the sons of Zion against the children of the Greeks, shall be their victory, as the Greek generations are consumed by those raised up against them, like archers straightly casting stones, so that the stone-throwers might be filled, drinking their blood very eagerly by the...

title: The Shepherd and the Living Stones
english: While they are sling-stoning and filling the altars like bowls.

When the sons of the Greeks suffer the things lying before them, such as being driven into stones and their blood being poured out, the Lord will save such as many as stand guard as having become a people like sheep; for after that, the powerful stones will become movable, having been built up with the divine foundation, so as to roll upon the earth of God, becoming light and movable as the weight and stoniness is lifted from them. For so, rolling upon the holy earth of God, they will build themselves up, harmoniously stepping into the walls of the holy city and the building of the temple of God.
What is meant by the being driven into stones by slings, those being consumed by those standing guard under God the Pantokrator, should be contemplated.

The corrective words of rebuke, like stones sent straight by a sling, will consume the sinners, so that they are no longer enemies of God, the wickedness having been consumed through which they were opposed to the grace of God, after they were struck down by the stones of the sling being made against them. For just as 'love covers a multitude of sins' (1 Pet 4:8) does not allow them to remain, having hidden the sins by making them vanish from all, so the rebuking and corrective words coming upon them, by which they are sling-stoned, will cover them, becoming their covering, the pouring out of the wine-like blood of them being a joy, as to gladden and pour out abundantly those who are pouring, so as to become altars, bowls, vessels of joy serving for use.

For how does one not partake of the divine, he who offers a sacrifice of praise and righteousness? For just as those performing the rite in an improper way cover the altar with tears, the most corrective [voice] saying to them: 'You covered my altar with tears; is it still worthy to look upon your sacrifice, or to receive a gift from your hands?' (Mal 2:13) Let these things be said to those sacrificing after impiety; but to those performing the rite piously, as their sacrifices are to be acceptable, the altars will be bowls making joy, so that, having been made sacred, they may be saved, being revealed in a luminous state, on the intellectual day, when they shall be saved, being transformed into a people of God like sheep.

For the first state of those beginning well and as they ought, is to be led like a flock by the best shepherd, so that after these things, having been promoted from sheep to a people, they might be made kings by the one who was previously their shepherd; those who, after being enriched, shall be a people of the Pantokrator and parts of the city being built by the Lord of Powers.

Stones that were rolling upon the earth of God because they had become hollow and light, being placed upon an immovable foundation, having become stones, build; Peter, the spokesman of the apostles, writes: 'To whom approaching, a chosen precious stone by God, and you yourselves, as living stones, are being built into a spiritual house for a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ' (1 Peter 2:5).

If concerning such ones those who give glory say, 'If these should be silent, the stones would cry out,' they proclaim holiness and the glory of God's earth, which all sings to Him, having worshiped Him, according to that which is written in the Psalms, where it says, 'Sing to the Lord, all the earth' (Ps 95:1), and where it says, 'Let all the earth worship you and sing to you' (Ps 66:4).

Taking the 'overflowing like wine' (Zech 9:17), the shoulder and toward slaughter were sought by those being consumed, casting it with the word in battle and in the stance of wars, seven books concerning the wise man.
Zechariah 9:17: That if there is anything good, it is His; and if anything beautiful, it is from Him, grain for youths and fragrant wine for virgins.

That which is principally acceptable and good exists, and that which is uncontradictedly praised is found, agreeing with the prophetic word in the epistle concerning him: 'Every good gift and every perfect gift comes down from above from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning' (Jas 1:17).
